# Source: https://github.com/openwrt/mt76/issues/732
# Title: SFP1 Port of Mediatek MT7986 / Banana Pi BPI-R3 not receiving traffic
# Retrieved: 2026-07-02
# License: user-posted content on GitHub, unclear
# Note: extracted from issue page embedded JSON

Banana Pi BPI-R3 has 2 SFP Ports. One (sfp2 - LAN) is connected via MT7531E and the other one (sfp1 - WAN) is connected directly via MT7986. Im running Openwrt Snapshot git-22.361.69865-deed682 (Build date 11.1.2023).

I inserted a SFP Fibre Transceiver Modul. Everything looks ok. Link is up. All debug messages (details see below) looks ok too. It is sending DHCP requests via this interface, but it is not receiving any packages back.

The firbre connection itself works fine. I confirmed this by inserting the cable in my Mikrotik Hex S, running openwrt 22.03.03 and using the same SFP Module. Here I get traffic back and getting a IP Adress via DHCP.

Below are my logs and ethtool outputs

btw. I'm getting the message "Host does not support 2.0W modules, module left in power mode 1" on my Mikrotik Hex S too. So I guess this is not relevant for the problem.

--------------

<p dir="auto">Banana Pi BPI-R3 has 2 SFP Ports. One (sfp2 - LAN) is connected via MT7531E and the other one (sfp1 - WAN) is connected directly via MT7986. Im running Openwrt Snapshot git-22.361.69865-deed682 (Build date 11.1.2023).</p>
<p dir="auto">I inserted a SFP Fibre Transceiver Modul. Everything looks ok. Link is up. All debug messages (details see below) looks ok too. It is sending DHCP requests via this interface, but it is not receiving any packages back.</p>
<p dir="auto">The firbre connection itself works fine. I confirmed this by inserting the cable in my Mikrotik Hex S, running openwrt 22.03.03 and using the same SFP Module. Here I get traffic back and getting a IP Adress via DHCP.</p>
<p dir="auto">Below are my logs and ethtool outputs</p>
<p dir="auto">btw. I'm getting the message "Host does not support 2.0W modules, module left in power mode 1" on my Mikrotik Hex S too. So I guess this is not relevant for the problem.</p>
